findings.evidence: Basic.lean:134 `have : T0Space S := hS.t0Space`; Basic.lean:141-142 uses `hf.isClosed_range.isComplete`; Mathlib `IsClosed.isComplete [CompleteSpace α] {s : Set α} (h : IsClosed s) : IsComplete s` has no T2/T0 hypothesis.
findings.fix: Drop "complete Hausdorff" and the "This is where Hausdorffness of the codomain does its work" sentence here; say instead that closedness of the range gives completeness and that separatedness (`T0Space`) is inherited along the embedding. Where Hausdorffness is actually used remains the equalizer proof in `Limits.lean`.
findings.issue: The docstring of `IsCompleteSeparated.of_isClosedEmbedding` says "the image is a closed subring of a complete Hausdorff ring, hence complete ... This is where Hausdorffness of the codomain does its work". The proof uses only `T0Space S` (line 134) to transport separatedness along the embedding; the completeness step is `IsUniformInducing.completeSpace` + `IsClosed.isComplete`, which needs no separation axiom (`Mathlib/Topology/UniformSpace/Cauchy.lean:451`: `theorem IsClosed.isComplete [CompleteSpace α]`). Hausdorffness is used in `Limits.lean:85-87` (`T2Space (F.obj .one)` for `isClosed_eq`), which `Limits.lean:19-20` correctly states — so the two files added by this PR contradict each other.

findings.evidence: Basic.lean:44-46 vs. Limits.lean:19-22 ("The equalizer closure is where separatedness of the codomain is used").
findings.fix: Restate as: closed subobjects of complete separated objects are complete separated; the Hausdorffness input sits in the equalizer closure that consumes it.
findings.issue: Same misattribution repeated in the module docstring bullet for `of_isClosedEmbedding`: "This is where Hausdorffness does its work, and the equalizer closure in `CompleteSeparated/Limits.lean` is its consumer."

findings.fix: Write `CategoryTheory.Limits.createsLimitFullSubcategoryInclusionOfClosed` (or name the instance actually driving synthesis, `CategoryTheory.Limits.hasLimitsOfShape_of_closedUnderLimits`, as the in-file comment at line 105 does).
findings.issue: Module docstring cites "Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.createsLimitFullSubcategoryInclusionOfClosed`". No such declaration exists under that namespace; it is `CategoryTheory.Limits.createsLimitFullSubcategoryInclusionOfClosed`. A reader grepping the cited name finds nothing, and the doc link does not resolve.

summary: Two docstring inaccuracies: the module docstring of `Limits.lean` cites a Mathlib declaration under a namespace it does not live in, and the `of_isClosedEmbedding` docs (lemma + module bullet) claim Hausdorffness does its work there, contradicting both the proof and `Limits.lean`'s own docstring.
